confidant

/KON-fih-dant/ - the stress falls on KON · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Confidant means a person trusted with private matters.

Every queen in the old dramas has her confidant — the one servant who hears the plans that the court must never learn.

Example

The climber's expedition journals named sponsors and route-mates, but her doubts went to a single confidant: a childhood friend in Lisbon who received a letter from every base camp and never showed one to anyone.

A confidant is defined by what is entrusted. A friend shares your table and an ally shares your battles, but a confidant holds your private matters — the doubts, plans, and secrets you say to exactly one person.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

intimate: An intimate is a close personal companion — someone woven into your daily life — whether or not secrets ever change hands. A confidant is defined by exactly that exchange: the one person trusted with your private matters. Every confidant is close, but not every close companion is a confidant.

ally: An ally is on your side in a fight — the teammate who defends you, the nation that joins your war — but an ally is not necessarily in the know. A confidant may take no side at all; what defines a confidant is being trusted with private matters.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

stranger: knows nothing of you at all

gossip: the last person anyone trusts with a secret

Where it sits · how deep the trust runs

acquaintance → friend → confidant

acquaintance vs. confidant: An acquaintance sits far below a confidant — you know the name, the face, the weather talk, and nothing private ever changes hands.

friend vs. confidant: Friend stops short of confidant: a friend shares your time and your table, while a confidant is trusted with the matters you tell no one else.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — con-: with, fully

Root — fid-: to trust (Latin fidere)

Suffix — -ant: a person who

Put it together: Latin fidere meant 'to trust,' and confidere was to trust wholly. Add -ant, 'a person,' and a confidant is literally 'a person trusted-with' — a human safe-deposit box. The same root steadies confide, the verb for placing a secret in that person's keeping.

Use the root in a new word: confide: By spring, the new lieutenant had found no one on the base to confide in.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / storybook-formal

Confidant is the precise word for the person on the receiving end of secrets — biographies and dramas lean on it. Friend measures affection and ally measures allegiance; confidant measures trust with private matters. (Spelled confidante, it is the traditional feminine form of the very same word.)
